title: validate init-project reasoning on real material set
goal: Run init-project phase1 against an in-repo real-material-derived project fixture and verify Q1 Q2 Q5 Q6 Q11 remain stable outside the tiny fixture.

acceptance.text: A real-material-derived in-repo project fixture returns stable answered_questions for Q1 Q2 Q5 Q6 Q11
Evidence updated for the validation run

key_updates: Added a richer in-repo real-material-derived fixture for init-project phase1 validation.
Validated that first-round answered_questions stay stable for Q1 Q2 Q5 Q6 Q11 outside the tiny toy fixture.
Tightened the Q6 heuristic so real-material README and docs can trigger a stable first-round workflow answer.
Filtered README command-path examples out of readme_refs_missing_in_repo so foundation tool commands no longer appear as missing repo files.
decisions: Use an in-repo real-material-derived fixture instead of external project roots for ongoing generic init-project reasoning validation.
Keep phase1 fail-closed even when five questions are answered; ready_for_doc_write remains false until follow-up reads are completed.
risks: Question-level reasoning still depends on explicit document cues and remains intentionally conservative for the remaining questions.
verification: python3 tools/init.py with project_root temporarily pointed at fixtures/init_project_real_material_fixture
python3 tools/appserverclient.py --init-project -new returned err_code=1012 with answered_questions covering Q1 Q2 Q5 Q6 Q11
python3 tools/appserverclient.py --init-project -new after command-path filtering returned readme_refs_missing_in_repo=[]
python3 tools/project_config.py after restoration confirmed project_root returned to /root/quant-factory-os
next_steps: Continue expanding phase1 answered_questions only when stable evidence exists, instead of adding broad heuristics.

conflict_policy.escalation_rule: if conflict remains, escalate to run-main
